common.description: the library dependency's own values, which helm adds under its name; leave it empty

enabled.description: read only by the `cluster-configs/stack` umbrella chart, which turns each node on or off with it

create.description: render a ServiceAccount named after the chart

name.x-default: chart name, or `default` when not created

automountToken.description: also applied to the pod spec

clusterRules.description: when set, a ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding for the ServiceAccount

rules.description: when set, a Role and RoleBinding in the release namespace

scope.description: `namespace` renders no ClusterRole or ClusterRoleBinding: `clusterRules` is ignored and `namespaceRules` joins `rules` in the Role, for a namespace that forbids cluster-scoped RBAC

namespaceRules.description: with `scope: namespace`, added to the Role in place of `clusterRules`: the namespaced part of what the app reads cluster-wide

x-doc-rows.description: render a DaemonSet; see DaemonSet below
merged over the base selector labels on the DaemonSet's selector and pods
the same pod, scheduling, container and volume keys as `deployment`, except `replicas` and `strategy`

probes.description: timings filled into each probe a container declares, under the container's own keys; a container without a probe gets none

enabled.description: render a `policy/v1` PodDisruptionBudget selecting the Deployment's pods

minAvailable.description: a count or a percentage; set to `null` to use `maxUnavailable`

maxUnavailable.description: a count or a percentage; mutually exclusive with `minAvailable`

enabled.description: render an `autoscaling/v2` HorizontalPodAutoscaler targeting the Deployment

targetCPUUtilizationPercentage.description: average CPU utilization, relative to the containers' CPU requests

enabled.description: render a Service selecting the Deployment's pods once `ports` lists one; `false` renders none

host.description: the key under `global.exposure.hosts` this app is reachable on, once `global.exposure.enabled` is true: an Ingress with `global.mesh: kubernetes`, a Gateway and VirtualService with `istio`

port.description: the name of the `service.ports` entry the host routes to

annotations.description: annotations on the Ingress, such as a controller's body-size limit

enabled.description: set `false` to leave this app out when `global.networkPolicy.enabled`

podSelector.description: a full label selector for the pods the policy covers, or a templated string that renders one; empty selects `app.kubernetes.io/name: <name>`

ingress.description: NetworkPolicy ingress rules, a list or a templated string; see Network policies

egress.description: NetworkPolicy egress rules after DNS (and istiod under `istio`), a list or a templated string

configMaps.description: a ConfigMap: `data` (map of file name to a string or a YAML object, templated) and/or `files` (a glob relative to the node chart, not templated)

keys.description: the keys an `ExternalSecret` fills when `global.externalSecrets.enabled`, which then replaces this Secret; `external.remoteKey` overrides the remote path

objects.description: any other manifest, such as a custom resource; templated, with name, namespace and labels filled in; skipped when the body renders empty

enabled.description: deliver every container's `secretEnv` through the Vault Agent Injector instead of `secretKeyRef`; see Secrets below

role.description: the Vault Kubernetes auth role the pod logs in as

path.description: KV v2 prefix; a secret is read from `<path>/<secretEnv.secret>`, field `<secretEnv.key>`, or from `<path>/<secret>` when `secret` is set

secret.description: one parent record every app reads, such as `OBS_SECRET`: each `secretEnv` entry then reads field `<Secret name>-<key>` of `<path>/<secret>` (`clickhouse-reader-password`), unless it sets `vault.field`; empty reads one record per Secret name

retention.description: how long the stack keeps each signal, in days; ClickHouse's TTLs and Cerberus's metadata lookback both read it, so they stay aligned

mesh.description: the service mesh the cluster runs: `istio` or `kubernetes`; anything else fails the render. `istio` renders a DestinationRule (`ISTIO_MUTUAL`) for every Service and, with exposure on, a Gateway and VirtualService per app; `kubernetes` renders none of them, and an Ingress for exposure

dataplaneMode.description: with `mesh: istio`, how pods join the mesh: `sidecar`, an istio-proxy in each pod and DestinationRules for `ISTIO_MUTUAL`; `ambient`, no sidecar, ztunnel carrying traffic over HBONE (15008), which every NetworkPolicy then allows between the same peers, and no DestinationRules

name.description: with `ambient`, an existing waypoint every Service uses for L7 policy (`istio.io/use-waypoint`); empty uses none. The stack never renders a waypoint

namespace.description: the waypoint's namespace when it is not the stack's (`istio.io/use-waypoint-namespace`)

imageRegistry.description: prepended to every image, so `registry.example/mirror` turns `grafana/grafana:13.2.2` into `registry.example/mirror/grafana/grafana:13.2.2`. An image that names its own registry keeps it in the path (`registry.example/mirror/ghcr.io/...`), which is how pull-through mirrors lay them out. Empty uses each image as written. Nodes that render images outside the common Deployment, such as ClickHouse's Installation and backup job, use the same `common.image` helper

shared.description: `false`: the stack installs the Altinity operator itself, as the `clickhouse-operator` application with its CRDs, ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding. `true`: a platform team already runs one that watches the stack's namespace; the app-of-apps renders no `clickhouse-operator` Application and the stack nothing cluster-scoped for ClickHouse. The operator's namespace is `global.networkPolicy.namespaces.operator`

podLabels.description: labels that select the operator's pods, for the ClickHouse NetworkPolicy and `make cluster/preflight`; a platform's operator installed from Altinity's Helm chart is usually `{app.kubernetes.io/name: altinity-clickhouse-operator}`

external.description: `false`: the stack runs ClickHouse, as the `clickhouse` application's ClickHouseInstallation. `true`: a service owner runs it at `global.services.clickhouse`; the app-of-apps renders no `clickhouse-operator` Application, the `clickhouse` node renders only its schema Job, and NetworkPolicies allow that address's port instead of the operator's pods

standalone.description: `true`: the `clickhouse` node runs ClickHouse as a single-replica Deployment with a PersistentVolumeClaim and a Service instead of a ClickHouseInstallation, so there is no operator and no CRD; the app-of-apps renders no `clickhouse-operator` Application. Fails with `external`. ClickHouse then serves only TLS (native `9440`, HTTPS `8443`) and every client verifies it, so `global.services.clickhouse` must be `<host>:9440` and `tls.serverName`, `tls.caConfigMap` and `tls.serverSecret` are required

networkPolicyPeers.description: with `external`, the NetworkPolicy peers (`ipBlock`, `namespaceSelector`, ...) `global.services.clickhouse` resolves to; empty allows its port to any destination

serverName.description: with `external` or `standalone`, required: the name the server's certificate must carry. Every client connects over TLS and verifies it; there is no option to skip verification, and no client presents a certificate of its own

caConfigMap.description: with `external` or `standalone`, required: a ConfigMap in the stack's namespace with the CA bundle that signed the server's certificate. The platform or the service owner provides it; the stack never creates a certificate

caKey.description: the key of the CA bundle in `caConfigMap`

serverSecret.description: with `standalone`, required: the `kubernetes.io/tls` Secret in the stack's namespace with the server's certificate and key (`tls.crt`, `tls.key`), which the platform provides; with `vault.enabled` on the `clickhouse` node, the Vault record of that name holds them instead. The stack never issues a certificate

requireLimits.description: the namespace has a ResourceQuota on CPU and memory, so every container, init containers and Jobs included, needs a CPU and memory request and limit; `make check/manifests` fails the environment's render on one without, and on a Vault agent without its resource annotations. Renders nothing itself

resources.description: every container's requests and limits unless it sets its own; a container's `resources` override these key by key, so a container that sets only `limits.memory` keeps these requests. An environment resizes every app here

imagePullSecrets.description: Secret names put on every pod that sets no `imagePullSecrets` of its own. A workload's list replaces this one, as Helm does for lists

vault.description: the same keys as `vault`, for every app at once; an app's own `vault` wins

clickhouse.description: where the collector, Cerberus, garmr and the schema Job reach ClickHouse's native protocol, as `host:port`; with `global.clickhouse.external`, the service owner's endpoint (`9440` is the usual TLS port)

otlpGrpc.description: where the demo load sends OTLP over gRPC

sqlAdapter.description: where vmalert sends its ClickHouse SQL rules

garmr.description: where Alertmanager sends notifications to garmr serve

alertHistory.description: where Alertmanager posts every notification so it is kept in otel_logs

enabled.description: render an `ExternalSecret` in place of every Secret in `secrets` that has `external.keys`

secretStoreRef.description: the store the site runs; an enabled render fails without a name

remotePath.description: a Secret is read from `<remotePath>/<Secret name>`, one property per key

refreshInterval.description: how often the operator re-reads the store

enabled.description: make the apps that set `exposure.host` reachable from outside the cluster

api.description: how exposure is rendered: `istio`, an Istio Gateway and VirtualService per app; `gateway-api`, an HTTPRoute per app on the Gateway API Gateway `gateway.name` names, which the platform runs and whose `allowedRoutes` admits this namespace; `ingress`, an Ingress. Empty follows the mesh: `istio`, or `ingress` with `kubernetes`

scheme.description: the scheme of the public URLs, such as Grafana's root URL; empty is `https` with `tls.credentialName` and `http` without. Set `https` when a platform Gateway terminates TLS

hosts.description: the hostname for each key an app can name in `exposure.host`, such as `grafana` or `otlp`; an enabled exposure fails the render when an app's host is empty

ingressClassName.description: the Ingress class; empty uses the cluster default

credentialName.description: a TLS Secret the site creates, used for every exposed host; empty serves plain HTTP. With Istio, the Secret lives in the ingress gateway's namespace (usually `istio-system`)

name.description: with `istio`, an existing Gateway to bind every VirtualService to, and with `gateway-api`, required: the platform's Gateway API Gateway every HTTPRoute attaches to. Either way no Gateway is rendered. Empty gives each app its own Gateway for its own host (443 with a TLS credential, 80 without)

namespace.description: the namespace of that existing Gateway

sectionName.description: with `gateway-api`, the Gateway listener every HTTPRoute attaches to; empty attaches to every listener that admits it

selector.description: which ingress gateway pods the rendered Gateways select

enabled.description: render a NetworkPolicy for every app; see Network policies

exposureNamespaces.description: namespaces whose pods may reach an exposed app (the ingress gateway or controller)

istioNamespace.description: where istiod runs, for the sidecar's egress under `mesh: istio`

namespaces.description: the stack's and the operator's namespaces, for rules that cross between them

enabled.description: render the workload once it lists containers: on by default for `deployment`, off for `daemonset`

reloader.description: annotate the Deployment for Stakater Reloader, so a changed Secret or ConfigMap rolls it; see Rollouts

replicas.description: omitted when `autoscaling.enabled`; see Disruption budget and autoscaling

podSecurityContext.description: merged key by key under a node's own, so a node sets only what it adds, such as runAsUser

nodeSelector.description: passed through to the pod spec; omitted when empty

affinity.description: passed through to the pod spec; omitted when empty

tolerations.description: passed through to the pod spec; omitted when empty

topologySpreadConstraints.description: passed through to the pod spec; omitted when empty

imagePullSecrets.description: a list of Secret names, rendered as `{name: <secret>}` entries; replaces `global.imagePullSecrets`, and omitted when both are empty

volumes.description: a volume source, such as `configMap: {name: ...}` or `emptyDir: {}`; templated. A string is templated and used as the whole source, so it can hold an `if`

if.description: templated; the entry is left out when it renders empty or false
